newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia stocks end mixed ahead of local holidays.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks end mixed ahead of local holidays.

text.p: Asia stock markets ended narrowly mixed on Thursday due to a variety of local factors and traders' reluctance to latch on to Wall Street's overnight rally ahead of market holidays in many centres.
Tokyo stocks see-sawed throughout the session before ending with a modest gain of 62.21 points, or 0.35 percent, at 18,093.41.
"The Nikkei 225 was pinned to 18,000 for most of the session, amid a tussle between profit-taking and buying back," said Masaaki Higashida, deputy general manager at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
In Hong Kong, stocks forfeited small, early gains to end slightly lower amid concern over the outlook for property developers and a reassessment of the interest rate outlook.
"The volatility in the market today is a symptom of investor's unease over interest rates and inflationary expectations," said Julian Ings Chambers, sales director at BZW Securities Asia.
The Hang Seng Index ended at 12,516,23, up 65.08 points, or 0.52 percent.

Despite a nearly 93 point rise in the Dow Jones Industrial Index overnight, the Hong Kong market had focused on the latest U.S. economic data, which rekindled talk the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates again.

For Hong Kong, a larger than expected rise in March U.S. industrial production and a sharp gain in capacity utilisation overshadowed news that U.S. tobacco companies were negotiating a settlement of massive health-related claims against them.
That news had pulled tobacco stocks -- and the overall market -- sharply higher.
The rally provided inspiration for Malaysian stocks, which broke out of a week-long slump and were up 16.80 points, or 1.54 percent at 1,104.58 in late trading.

Stocks in the Philippines retreated, however, following a sharp drop in the price of blue chip Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) in New York overnight and renewed concerns over the property sector.
PLDT ended 10 pesos lower at 1,545 pesos.
"All the bad news we've had over the past two weeks came into play today and most investors decided to sell off," said Teresa Lee, vice president at Asiamerit Securities.

In Thailand, stocks traced a sharp drop in troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) when its shares resumed trading after an 11 month suspension. "Looking at the balance sheet of BBC last week, I don't see any value," one trader said.
The market struggled to maintain the key 700 level throughout the session and was off 15.13 points, or 2.11 percent, at 701.76 in late trading.

Taiwan stocks closed lower as investors fled to the sidelines amid concern over a government plan to accelerate the sale of shares in state-run commercial banks. The government's move to add supply to the market was seen as a deliberate bid to cool the market's advance.

News of the plan overshadowed the rise on Wall Street and news that Beijing had approved six Taiwan shipping firms to sail directly across the Taiwan strait for the first time since 1949. The weighted index ended 122.68 points, or 1.42 percent, lower at 8,492.10.
Elsewhere in Asia, Indonesian shares were up 4.775 points, or 0.75 percent, at 637.594.

Stocks in Singapore were little changed, with the 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index up 3.01 points, or 0.15 percent, at 2,043.20, while Australia's All Ordinaries Index ended up 6.8 points, or 0.28 percent, at 2,413.2. New Zealand shares were off 1.53 points at 2,252.01.
